LEARNING PATH · CLASS 44 · POSITION & DIRECTION WORDS · AGES 4–5

Prepositions for kids — twenty-two printable position & direction word cards to act out.

Twenty-two printable position and direction flashcards for ages four to five, all on this one page, in four shelves. Up and down, above and below, over and under, inside and outside, across and through: the words that tell you WHERE. Every card shows the word five ways with labeled pictures, so the word sticks the way a game sticks — and every word has something your body can do right now, downloading and printing straight from this page. Pick a card, print it, and the hallway becomes a treasure map.

Back to the Learning Path ↗
HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

One little word. Your whole body does it. That is the lesson.

Position words are the first math words a child ever uses — before numbers, comes WHERE. Every card in this class prints one word five ways: the word big at the top, then five labeled pictures showing it — balloon above, book above, bird above. You do not need a desk for this class. You need a floor, a table to crawl under, and maybe a sock to toss over your shoulder. Say the word, do the word, and the word is yours.

The shelves follow how the words grow. The Up & Down shelf starts with the ones your body already knows — jumping up, flopping down, hiding under. Where Things Are adds the hiding words — inside, outside, between, next to, in front of, back-behind. The Way Things Move puts directions in your feet — across, around, through, toward, away from. And Sides & Distance finishes with the two tricky teams — left and right, near and far — that later become maps, dances and driving directions.

THE UP & DOWN SHELF · 7 CARDS

Words your body already knows.

Printable position word flashcards for preschool and up: up, down, above, below, over, under and on — the first positional words kids act out with their whole bodies, one card each with a way to try it today. Every card carries its four pills — age, subject, grade level, skill — and its Download + Print buttons right under the picture, straight from this page.

THE WHERE THINGS ARE SHELF · 6 CARDS

Inside, outside, in between.

Where-things-are flashcards for ages 4–5: inside and outside, between and next to, in front of and back-behind — the position words that turn "where is it?" into a game a four-year-old wins. Every card carries its four pills — age, subject, grade level, skill — and its Download + Print buttons right under the picture, straight from this page.

THE WAY THINGS MOVE SHELF · 5 CARDS

Direction words with feet on them.

Printable direction flashcards: across, around, through, toward and away from — movement words for preschool and kindergarten that turn the hallway into an obstacle course of words. Every card carries its four pills — age, subject, grade level, skill — and its Download + Print buttons right under the picture, straight from this page.

THE SIDES & DISTANCE SHELF · 4 CARDS

Near, far and your two sides.

Left and right, near and far — the comparison words that grow into map skills, dancing directions and crossing the street safely, each on its own printable card. Every card carries its four pills — age, subject, grade level, skill — and its Download + Print buttons right under the picture, straight from this page.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where the position words grow up.

Opposite pairs in Class 19 · Age 3 ↗Neighborhood walks in Class 33 · Ages 4–5 ↗Measuring & Money in Class 42 · Ages 4–5 ↗The Learning Path ↗

Class 19 compares — big and little, more and less, over and under in its own opposite pairs — and this class hands those pairs their real names. Class 33 walks the neighborhood, where every walk is a direction word: toward the mailbox, across the street, next to the park. Class 42 measures and sorts, and its own shelf already keeps a few position words — this class is where those words get a whole school day. And when you want the next class, the Learning Path holds all forty-nine in order — and the whole deck prints again from the Prepositions parents’ shelf.

Position words are caught, not taught. Every card here hands you a word your body can try before your brain has to — and your grown-up’s whole job is to say it out loud with you while you do it.
